stem.text: An open-top baking pan is made from a rectangular sheet of tin 35 decimeters by 56 decimeters by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The baking pan can be at most 5 decimeters tall. Find the largest possible volume of the baking pan, in cubic decimeters.

worked_solution.text: The baking pan has height x and a base \( 35 - 2 x \) by \( 56 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(35 - 2 x\right)\left(56 - 2 x\right) \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 5, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 5 \).
\( V'(x) = 4 \left(x - 7\right) \left(3 x - 70\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 7 \) and \( x = \frac{70}{3} \); only \( x = 7 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 7 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 5 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 5 \).
The largest volume is \( V(5) = 5\left(25\right)\left(46\right) = 5750 \) cubic decimeters.

options.derivation: the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 7 is used
the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
